explanation: The statement concerns `KTheory.ProjectiveClass.tensorMul`, a noncomputable binary operation defined in this library on the library's own `ProjectiveClass R` (a localization of the skeleton of finite projective right modules). Grepping Mathlib for `tensorMul`, `tensorClass`, `ProjectiveClass`, `RightProjective`, `K0` and `KTheory` finds no such constructions: Mathlib has no algebraic K-theory of projective modules and no `ProjectiveClass`. The only Mathlib ingredient used in the proof is `TensorProduct.comm` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean), the general commutativity equivalence `M ⊗ N ≃ₗ N ⊗ M`, which is not the theorem's content — the content lies in the library's own definition of `tensorMul` and its descent through `induction_on`/`of_eq_of_equiv`. The derive-from-`mul_comm` route would only be available after the `CommSemiring` instance is built, which depends on this very theorem, so it is circular. Hence no Mathlib duplicate or single-declaration special case exists.
